contradictions.claim: Brighton Fringe leadership acted independently of any criminal implications in removing Ben Carter.
contradictions.reality: Despite being aware of a live crime reference (47250093423) against Duncan Lustig-Prean for stalking and harassment, Brighton Fringe refused to acknowledge this or factor it into their board decision-making. Duncan retained sole control over the board minutes, while Sussex Police had already assigned an investigating officer (PC Alan Russell).

contradictions.claim: Brighton Fringe board acts collectively and transparently in governance decisions.
contradictions.reality: Duncan Lustig-Prean admits that the board minutes regarding Ben Carter’s removal have yet to be written and that he alone will approve and redact the record. This follows a refusal to confirm any audio/video record of the meeting, no confirmation of attendance list, and a failure to disclose legal basis or policy. Duncan’s gatekeeping of records following a safeguarding disclosure indicates rewriting of events after the fact — in breach of trustee obligations.

contradictions.claim: Brighton Fringe board had all relevant safeguarding and legal information when making decisions regarding Ben Carter’s removal.
contradictions.reality: A second crime reference number (47250152583) was issued by Sussex Police for stalking and harassment on 3 August 2025. This was submitted independently and without the knowledge of Brighton Fringe Chair Duncan Lustig-Prean, after the board refused to engage with Ben's disclosures or the initial police assignment (CR 47250093423). The new report was routed through policeplease.com, circumventing institutional obstruction.
laws_breached: Human Rights Act 1998 (Right to fair treatment and remedy)

timeline.event: Sussex Police formally confirm Ben Carter as the victim in Crime Reference 47250093423, with PC Alan Russell assigned as investigating officer.
